conventions.convention: The Conway polynomial is normalized by ∇U=1 and ∇L+−∇L−=z∇L0, using oriented smoothing. Its separately prescribed empty-link value is zero.
Height increases upward; integration levels satisfy tmin<t_m<⋯<t_1<tmax. The pairing sign counts endpoints where height decreases along the skeleton orientation.
Closed framed diagrams impose 4T; closed unframed diagrams also kill isolated chords. The unframed tangle quotient kills chords with consecutive endpoints on one skeleton component.
KZ transport uses Ωq=(2πi)⁻¹Σtij dlog(zi−zj); later path segments multiply on the left, and the positive half-turn has transport exp(tij/2).
The fixed hump H has two local maxima, r(K) counts maxima, and I(K)=Z(K)Z(H)⁻ʳ⁽ᴷ⁾. The target is the complexification of rational diagram spaces; rationality of coefficients is not asserted.
Configuration cells use orientation dt1∧⋯∧dtm; boundary orientations are outward-normal-first, with Morse coordinate t−c=±s² at critical levels.
Ambient-isotopy invariance, and the associated-graded and universality conclusions that consume it, assume countable choice.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the unframed configuration series Z, the KZ holonomy, tangential endpoint convention, and normalized series I(K)=Z(K)Z(H)⁻ʳ⁽ᴷ⁾.
Assume ACω. If K0 and K1 are related by a smooth ambient isotopy, then I(K0)=I(K1). For a fixed parenthesization, KZ holonomy is invariant under fixed-endpoint homotopies of the configuration path.

Under ACω and the stated common Morse-presentation hypotheses, the alternating integral of an n-singular knot has zero components below degree n and degree-n component exactly its unframed chord diagram D; for n=0 the degree-zero component is 1.
Each fixed-degree unframed configuration coefficient is absolutely convergent after the finite pairing sum in the quotient; the stated critical-needle contribution is bounded by Cmε.
For matched compact strict Morse tangles with smooth embedded composite, the unframed integrals converge absolutely degreewise and Z(T2∘T1)=Z(T2)Z(T1), with T2 stacked above T1.
Tangential KZ transport is uniquely regularized degreewise. Insertion of the specified hump gives Z(K+)=Z(H)Z(K) and r(K+)=r(K)+1, hence I(K+)=I(K).
Under countable choice, I≤n is type at most n and its n-fold finite difference on an n-singular knot with diagram D is D.

The second Conway coefficient has type at most two, with second derivative 1 on intersecting two-chord diagrams and 0 on nonintersecting diagrams; its unknot and specified positive-trefoil values are 0 and 1.

concerns.concern: The uniform needle bound lacks a uniform separation hypothesis. Step 1.2 says, “compactness and embeddedness give a uniform positive lower bound for |z-z′|,” but embeddedness for each ε and compact control of the critical-point charts do not prevent another regular strand from approaching the needle as ε→0. Locally take the fixed Morse cap z=s, t=−s², |s|≤ε/2, and another upward strand z=iε. The cap has horizontal diameter ε and its critical chart is unchanged. Its two signed degree-one mixed-chord integrals sum, up to orientation sign, to (2πi)⁻¹ log((1/2−i)/(−1/2−i)), a nonzero constant; the chord joins different skeleton components and survives tangle 1T. These local pieces can be extended by regular arcs inside a fixed slab. Thus the written chart assumptions do not justify Cmε uniformly. The cited CDM §8.6.2 argument also uses opposite-branch cancellation rather than the claimed individual absolute long-chord estimate. The convergence assertion for a fixed tangle is a separate issue.
